blocks.content:
You can create panels from a plain-language goal, or ask for an explanation of a dashboard you already have.

Choose one path now:

- **Option A: Create a draft dashboard** if you have metrics data to work with.
- **Option B: Explain an existing dashboard** if your stack has little data (open a dashboard you can view first).

Complete only the section for your choice. Skip every step in the other section.

whenTrue.content: If this guide is docked in the sidebar, pop it out into a floating window so it stays visible beside **Assistant**.

blocks.content:
Confirm your choice: **Option A** (create) or **Option B** (explain).

If you chose **Option B**, skip the whole Option A section that follows and continue at Option B.
To create a draft dashboard (**Option A**), complete the following steps:

blocks.title: Option A: Create a draft dashboard

blocks.content: If the Assistant panel is closed, open **Assistant** from the top toolbar.
blocks.hint: Skip this whole Option A section if you chose Option B, or skip this step if Assistant is already open.

blocks.content:
In the chat input, paste or type:

> Create a dashboard called 'Checkout Health' with panels for error rate, p95 latency, and request volume.

Mention data sources with the at symbol (@) when you can, for example a Prometheus source from the mention list.
blocks.hint: Skip if you chose Option B.
Skip if you chose Option B.

blocks.content:
Judge the draft before you save:

- **Useful draft:** The panels match the goal you asked for (for example error rate, latency, and volume), and data sources look right when `@` mentions were used.
- **Needs another pass:** Panels are missing, titles don't match the goal, or the draft isn't something you'd keep even as a starting point.

Don't treat an unsaved or unreviewed draft as production. Save only after a quick review, or send a follow-up to adjust panels first.
blocks.hint: Skip if you chose Option B.

blocks.content:
If you finished **Option A**, you should have a draft dashboard to review. You can skip the Option B section below.

If you chose **Option B**, make sure a dashboard is open, then complete the following steps:

blocks.title: Option B: Explain an existing dashboard

blocks.content: If the Assistant panel is closed, open **Assistant** from the top toolbar.
blocks.hint: Skip this whole Option B section if you chose Option A, or skip this step if Assistant is already open.

blocks.content:
In the chat input, paste or type:

> Explain what this dashboard shows.

Or use a panel menu Assistant action if available (**Explain in Assistant**, **Troubleshoot panel**, and similar), then skip **Send**.
blocks.hint: Skip if you chose Option A, or if you already used a panel menu action.

blocks.content: If you typed a prompt in chat, click **Send**.
blocks.hint: Skip if you chose Option A, or if you used a panel menu action instead.

blocks.content:
Judge whether the explanation maps to the open dashboard:

- **Useful:** It names panels or signals you can see on the dashboard, and the summary matches the layout in front of you.
- **Needs a follow-up:** It stays generic, or it doesn't match the panels on screen.

If it needs a follow-up, point at a specific panel title in your next prompt.
blocks.hint: Skip if you chose Option A.

blocks.content:
You should have either a reviewed draft dashboard or an explanation you checked against the open dashboard.

For more examples, refer to [Manage dashboards](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/machine-learning/assistant/guides/dashboarding/).

whenTrue.content: Dock this guide back to the sidebar when you are ready for the next milestone.

blocks.content: In the next milestone, you'll wrap up this path and see where to go next.
